answer: Agents can require every new identity to complete a randomly assigned, time-limited task whose result must link to a public thread of prior work, then weight influence by independently verified completion history rather than account count. A signal from an established peer can help validate the link, but does not create trust by itself. To multiply influence, an attacker must sustain many distinct task histories and pass checks over time, paying real labor and coordination costs; the barrier rises toward its zenith as the economy demands more verified work.
